written.myAnswer: The three general types of motion are translatory, rotatory and vibratory. In translatory motion, all points of a body move the same distance in the same direction over the same time; examples include a car (linear motion), a bee following an irregular path (random motion), and a Ferris wheel (circular motion). In rotatory motion, a body turns about a fixed axis; examples include an electric fan and a top. Vibratory motion is repeated to-and-fro motion about a fixed position; a swing is an example.
